result:
Review complete. The diff is small (3 files, +21/-2): a new `dataDir()` helper that redirects the LLM cache and analytics log to `/tmp` when `process.env.VERCEL` is set, plus the two call sites. I read the helper, both consumers (`persist.ts`, `cache.ts`), all callers (`callLlm.ts`, `streamLlm.ts`, `artifactRoute.ts`, `app/api/analytics/route.ts`, `useAnalytics.ts`), `.gitignore`, README, and the docker/verifier setup.

Note: the `ReportFindings` tool is not available in this session, so findings are stated directly below.

Core logic checks that passed: no other `process.cwd()`-based data paths were left behind (grep shows `dataDir.ts` is the only one); `data/` is gitignored, so there is no committed read-only data that would be shadowed by `/tmp`; every write path (`appendAnalyticsEntry`, `setCachedResult`, `removeCachedResult`) is already wrapped in try/catch by callers, so the path change cannot introduce new unhandled throws; `ensureDir()` on `/tmp` is a no-op-safe existsSync check; the refactor commit `b64c1ca` is behavior-identical to `2136fd6` (`/tmp/cache` and `/tmp/analytics.jsonl` unchanged); and these modules import `fs`, so they are server-only and not at risk of client-bundle env inlining.

Findings (all low severity — I found no correctness bug that breaks a normal request path):

- `/repo/app/lib/utils/dataDir.ts:13` — Truthiness test on `process.env.VERCEL` treats the strings `"0"` and `"false"` as "on Vercel". A self-hosted or CI deployment that explicitly sets `VERCEL=false` (a common way to disable Vercel-specific behavior) silently loses durable storage: the LLM cache and analytics log go to `/tmp` and vanish on restart, with no error. `process.env.VERCEL === "1"` would be exact.
- `/repo/app/lib/utils/dataDir.ts:13` — Redirecting the cache to `/tmp` introduces an unbounded-growth risk that did not exist before. Vercel Functions cap `/tmp` at 512 MB and `setCachedResult` never evicts; previously no writes landed at all on Vercel (EROFS, swallowed), so the cache could not fill anything. A warm container serving many distinct prompts (each cached response is a full JSON blob) can exhaust `/tmp`; cache-write ENOSPC is swallowed, but anything else in the container that needs `/tmp` then fails too. Some size cap or TTL sweep is warranted.
- `/repo/app/lib/analytics/persist.ts:8` — On Vercel, analytics are now per-container rather than universally empty, which makes the clear flow visibly incorrect. `DELETE /api/analytics` truncates `/tmp/analytics.jsonl` on whichever instance handles it; a later `GET` routed to a different warm container returns that container's entries, and because `refresh()` in `/repo/app/hooks/useAnalytics.ts:14` only calls `setEntries` when `data.entries.length > 0`, the user sees "cleared" analytics reappear on reload while a genuinely empty response leaves stale local state. Before this change the list was consistently empty on Vercel.
- `/repo/app/lib/analytics/persist.ts:6` — The comment points readers to a "Deploy to Vercel" section in the README, but the README has no such section and never mentions Vercel (headings: What is this? / Getting Started / Lean Verification Service / Available Scripts / How to Contribute / Project Documentation / Questions or Issues? / License). Either add the section or drop the cross-reference; as written it sends maintainers looking for documentation of the ephemerality tradeoff that does not exist.
